The Story of Charudatt

I bow to the lotus feet of Lord Jinendra, worshipped by the gods, and I write the story of the merchant Charudatt.

At the time of this story, Shursen was king of Champapuri — a wise ruler devoted to the welfare of his people. His just governance was praised by all. In that city lived a respected merchant named Bhanudatt, whose wife was Subhadra. Subhadra had no children, and in her desire for offspring she worshipped various gods and goddesses and took many vows. Yet her wish remained unfulfilled. Truly, has worship of false gods ever accomplished anything?

One day, when she went to the temple to see the Lord, she beheld a wandering monk there. She bowed to him and asked, "Lord, will my wish ever be fulfilled?" The monk, knowing the feelings of her heart, replied, "Daughter, the worship and vows you offer to false gods day and night are not right. Instead of gain, they bring only harm. Believe this — in this world, no deity can give or take anything apart from one's own merit and sin. Until now, your sinful karma was ascendant, so your desire could not be fulfilled. But now your great merit shall ripen, and you shall receive a precious son. For this, place your faith in the pure dharma born of merit."

Hearing the monk's prophecy, Subhadra was overjoyed. She bowed and returned home. From that day she abandoned all worship of false gods and began practising charity, worship, and vows in accordance with the Jain dharma. Her days passed in great happiness, and in time, as the monk had foretold, a son was born to her. He was named Charudatt. As he grew, noble qualities took root in him naturally. Truly, all good things come of their own accord to the fortunate.

From childhood, Charudatt devoted himself to study. Even at twenty-four or twenty-five, sensual desire had not touched him. His love was for books and learning. He became a great scholar, respected throughout the land. When the time came, he married a virtuous wife and continued to live a life of dharma, charity, and devotion to the Jinas. He gave generously to the worthy, worshipped daily, and inspired others to walk the righteous path.

In time Charudatt recognised the impermanence of worldly life. He renounced his possessions, became a monk, and through dedicated meditation and austerity, purified his soul and attained liberation.

This story teaches that true blessings come not from the worship of false gods but from the ripening of one's own merit, nurtured by right faith and righteous conduct. Subhadra's faith in the monk's word brought her a noble son, and Charudatt's devotion to learning and dharma led him ultimately to the supreme goal.
